assumptions: The NL states there are twelve finite states but does not provide their canonical names; descriptive state names were synthesized from the stated operating branches.

Because no exact diesel/LNG capacity taxonomy was supplied, Pgmax is treated as the LNG generator capacity, eng3_Pmax as a subsequent generating unit capacity, and Pd1max/Pd2max as DG1/DG2 capacities.

A battery maximum discharge variable Pbat_max was introduced to make the phrase 'batteries when SoC is suitable' operational; the NL names battery discharge power but does not give its capacity symbol.

The model is a condition-classification abstraction: forced guard transitions reselect the active dispatch state from current PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity inputs rather than storing historical mode memory.
The low-SoC threshold other than the stated full threshold 0.95 is not specified in the NL; SoC <= 0.2 was chosen as a conventional low-SoC abstraction.

The final all-thermal state covers both DG2 last-priority dispatch and the stated overload-mitigation branch; when demand exceeds all thermal capacity, battery discharge covers the remaining lack as described.
Load cut-in/cut-out commands are modeled coarsely from PL being positive or zero because the NL does not provide detailed load-shedding or load-restoration rules.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, the EMS serves all ship demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
Dispatch priority uses LNG before diesel units when RES is below load demand.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins in later diesel-generator cases.

decisions.rationale: Pbat_max is a preserved NL-grounded capacity/input abstraction for the battery discharge limit. The NL says the FSM reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not provide any update law for Pbat_max. Adding a write would invent plant/environment dynamics or a meaningless self-assignment, both forbidden by the request and repair rules.

The BatteryDischarge classification guard reads external operating inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_max. These are intended environmental/measurement inputs for dynamic reclassification, not internal state variables. No NL-grounded safe write is available.

The same BatteryDischarge forced guard from ZeroLoadSpare depends only on external ship-load, renewable, SoC, and battery-limit inputs. Changing the guard or adding writes would either remove required dispatch logic or invent unsupported input dynamics.

The RESCoversCharge to BatteryDischarge classification guard must remain driven by current external demand/resource/SoC/capacity values. There is no safe NL-grounded DSL edit that makes these inputs internally written without changing model meaning.

The RESCoversSpare to BatteryDischarge guard is a required forced reclassification condition over external operating inputs. The diagnostic is conservative for a condition-classification controller; no meaningful internal write is specified by the NL.

The self reclassification of BatteryDischarge is intentional because the EMS continuously classifies current external conditions. Adding artificial updates to PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, or Pbat_max would be ungrounded.

The LNGCoveredChargeLowSoC to BatteryDischarge guard preserves the required priority branch from thermal/charging operation back to battery discharge when current external conditions permit. No NL-grounded write exists for the guard variables.

The LNGCovered to BatteryDischarge guard is intentionally controlled by current external demand/resource/SoC/capacity inputs. Simplifying or removing it would reduce required dispatch coverage; adding writes would invent dynamics.

variable_role_summary.policy: Advisory only. Do not invent writes for external_input_candidate variables unless NL explicitly gives update semantics; add meaningful NL-grounded writes only for internal state variables.
variable_role_summary.source: SD-4 diagnostic refs and generic NL external-input rationale

decisions.rationale: Pbat_max is a preserved NL-grounded capacity/input abstraction for the battery discharge limit. The NL says the FSM reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not provide any update law for Pbat_max. Adding a write would invent plant/environment dynamics or a meaningless self-assignment, both forbidden by the request and repair rules.

The BatteryDischarge classification guard reads external operating inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_max. These are intended environmental/measurement inputs for dynamic reclassification, not internal state variables. No NL-grounded safe write is available.

The same BatteryDischarge forced guard from ZeroLoadSpare depends only on external ship-load, renewable, SoC, and battery-limit inputs. Changing the guard or adding writes would either remove required dispatch logic or invent unsupported input dynamics.

The RESCoversCharge to BatteryDischarge classification guard must remain driven by current external demand/resource/SoC/capacity values. There is no safe NL-grounded DSL edit that makes these inputs internally written without changing model meaning.

The RESCoversSpare to BatteryDischarge guard is a required forced reclassification condition over external operating inputs. The diagnostic is conservative for a condition-classification controller; no meaningful internal write is specified by the NL.

The self reclassification of BatteryDischarge is intentional because the EMS continuously classifies current external conditions. Adding artificial updates to PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, or Pbat_max would be ungrounded.

The LNGCoveredChargeLowSoC to BatteryDischarge guard preserves the required priority branch from thermal/charging operation back to battery discharge when current external conditions permit. No NL-grounded write exists for the guard variables.

The LNGCovered to BatteryDischarge guard is intentionally controlled by current external demand/resource/SoC/capacity inputs. Simplifying or removing it would reduce required dispatch coverage; adding writes would invent dynamics.

The LNGDG3ChargeLowSoC to BatteryDischarge guard is part of the preserved forced classification guard set. Its variables are external measurements or capacity bounds, so the warning should be waived rather than repaired by unsafe edits.
The LNGDG3Covered to BatteryDischarge guard correctly reads external operating inputs to dynamically switch dispatch states. The NL gives no update semantics for those inputs inside the EMS.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL candidate emitted because every requested design warning concerns intentional external-input reads; any syntactic repair would be ungrounded or would delete required dispatch classification logic.

repair_rationale: All requests target W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR or W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE for variables that are external operating inputs or capacity bounds in this condition-classification EMS.
The NL explicitly frames PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds as values the FSM reads. It does not specify internal dynamics for load, renewable generation, SoC evolution, or Pbat_max.
The repair rules forbid adding meaningless self-assignments or inventing plant/environment dynamics merely to silence warnings.

Preserved required elements include Pbat_max, all twelve dispatch states, forced classification guards, the RES/full-SoC guard, and low-SoC charging-margin guards. A DSL edit to remove or rewrite these guards would risk NL-fidelity regression.
Therefore the safe action is to reject these repair edits and rely on waiver/local override for intentional external-input guard variables.

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: with PL=0, positive RES, and SoC below 0.95, first empty cycle dispatches to zero-load battery charging.
scenario_results.name: default_zero_load_res_charges_battery

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: with PL=0 and SoC at the 0.95 boundary, RES production should become spare power instead of battery charge.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_full_soc_routes_res_to_spare

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when RES exceeds positive load and SoC is just below 0.95, EMS should serve load from RES and charge the battery.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: at SoC=0.95 with RES exceeding load, residual renewable power should be spare, not battery charge.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_full_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when RES is below load, SoC is above low threshold, and deficit fits battery capacity, battery discharge should cover the gap before thermal units.
scenario_results.name: battery_supplies_deficit_when_soc_suitable

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: at SoC=0.2, LNG-covered deficit should include the Pgmax/5 charging margin while staying within LNG capacity.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_covered_adds_pgmax_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: just above low SoC, a deficit within LNG capacity should be covered by LNG without a battery charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_covers_deficit_above_low_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: at low SoC, when LNG alone is insufficient but LNG+DG3 plus Pd1max/10 margin suffices, EMS should use LNG and DG3 and charge the battery.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_dg3_adds_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: above low SoC, when deficit exceeds LNG but fits LNG+DG3, EMS should request LNG first and DG3 for the residual without charging.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg3_covers_deficit_above_low_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: at low SoC, when LNG+DG3 are insufficient but adding DG1 with Pd1max/10 margin suffices, EMS should use LNG, DG3, DG1, and charge.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_dg3_dg1_adds_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: above low SoC, when deficit exceeds LNG+DG3 but fits LNG+DG3+DG1, DG1 should be used as later priority without charging.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg3_dg1_covers_deficit_above_low_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: if demand exceeds RES and all thermal capacity, all thermal units should be active and remaining lack covered by battery discharge.
scenario_results.name: extreme_demand_all_thermal_and_battery_mitigation

decisions.rationale: Pbat_max is an NL-grounded external capacity/input abstraction for the battery discharge limit. The NL says the FSM reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not provide any update law for Pbat_max. Adding a write would invent plant/environment dynamics or a meaningless self-assignment, both forbidden by the request and repair rules. This same issue was already rejected/waived in the FixLog and no new evidence changes that conclusion.

The BatteryDischarge classification guard from ZeroLoadCharge reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_max as current external operating inputs. These values are meant to be supplied by the ship/load/resource environment for dynamic reclassification, not internally evolved by the EMS. Adding writes would be ungrounded and removing the guard would delete required dispatch behavior.

The BatteryDischarge classification guard from ZeroLoadSpare depends on external load, renewable, SoC, and battery-limit inputs. The NL gives no safe internal update semantics for those variables. This was already waived in the previous FixLog, and the current request provides no new evidence requiring a DSL edit.

The RESCoversCharge to BatteryDischarge forced reclassification guard is required so the EMS can switch when current demand exceeds renewables and battery discharge is suitable. Its guard variables are external measurements/capacity inputs. A write-only repair would invent dynamics, while simplifying the guard would reduce required dispatch coverage.

The RESCoversSpare to BatteryDischarge guard is an NL-grounded condition-classification branch over current PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_max. These are external operating inputs in this model. No smallest safe edit can make them internally written without changing the model meaning.

The BatteryDischarge self-reclassification warning is expected for a forced classification controller that continuously rereads external operating conditions. Adding artificial updates to PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, or Pbat_max would violate the repair rule against inventing plant/environment dynamics.

The LNGCoveredChargeLowSoC to BatteryDischarge forced guard preserves the required priority transition back to battery discharge when current external conditions permit. The NL does not define internal updates for the guard variables, and deleting or weakening the guard would regress required dispatch behavior.

The LNGCovered to BatteryDischarge guard is intentionally controlled by external demand/resource/SoC/capacity values. The previous FixLog already rejected the same repair as unsafe; no new evidence supports adding a grounded write or simplifying this required classification guard.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL edit made. The requested warnings concern intentional external-input/capacity reads in required forced classification guards; repairing them would require ungrounded input dynamics or deletion/simplification of preserved dispatch logic.

repair_rationale: All current requests are repeats of warnings already rejected/waived in the FixLog: W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for Pbat_max and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE for BatteryDischarge classification guards.
The NL explicitly says the EMS reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not specify internal dynamics for ship load, renewable production, SoC evolution, or Pbat_max.

The selected diagnostics' variable_role_summary supports treating these guard variables as external-input candidates. Under the repair rules, external inputs should not receive invented writes merely to silence warnings.

The preserve list requires Pbat_max, all twelve states, forced_classification_guards, the RES/full-SoC guard, and low-SoC charging-margin guards. Editing away the guards or replacing them with constants would cause NL-fidelity/design regression.
Because no request can be safely accepted, no repaired candidate DSL is emitted.

variable_role_summary.policy: Advisory only. Do not invent writes for external_input_candidate variables unless NL explicitly gives update semantics; add meaningful NL-grounded writes only for internal state variables.
variable_role_summary.source: SD-4 diagnostic refs and generic NL external-input rationale

decisions.rationale: Pbat_max is an NL-grounded external capacity/input abstraction for the battery discharge limit. The NL says the FSM reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not provide any update law for Pbat_max. Adding a write would invent plant/environment dynamics or a meaningless self-assignment, both forbidden by the request and repair rules. This same issue was already rejected/waived in the FixLog and no new evidence changes that conclusion.

The BatteryDischarge classification guard from ZeroLoadCharge reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_max as current external operating inputs. These values are meant to be supplied by the ship/load/resource environment for dynamic reclassification, not internally evolved by the EMS. Adding writes would be ungrounded and removing the guard would delete required dispatch behavior.

The BatteryDischarge classification guard from ZeroLoadSpare depends on external load, renewable, SoC, and battery-limit inputs. The NL gives no safe internal update semantics for those variables. This was already waived in the previous FixLog, and the current request provides no new evidence requiring a DSL edit.

The RESCoversCharge to BatteryDischarge forced reclassification guard is required so the EMS can switch when current demand exceeds renewables and battery discharge is suitable. Its guard variables are external measurements/capacity inputs. A write-only repair would invent dynamics, while simplifying the guard would reduce required dispatch coverage.

The RESCoversSpare to BatteryDischarge guard is an NL-grounded condition-classification branch over current PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_max. These are external operating inputs in this model. No smallest safe edit can make them internally written without changing the model meaning.

The BatteryDischarge self-reclassification warning is expected for a forced classification controller that continuously rereads external operating conditions. Adding artificial updates to PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, or Pbat_max would violate the repair rule against inventing plant/environment dynamics.

The LNGCoveredChargeLowSoC to BatteryDischarge forced guard preserves the required priority transition back to battery discharge when current external conditions permit. The NL does not define internal updates for the guard variables, and deleting or weakening the guard would regress required dispatch behavior.

The LNGCovered to BatteryDischarge guard is intentionally controlled by external demand/resource/SoC/capacity values. The previous FixLog already rejected the same repair as unsafe; no new evidence supports adding a grounded write or simplifying this required classification guard.

The LNGDG3ChargeLowSoC to BatteryDischarge guard is part of the preserved forced_classification_guards element. Its variables are external measurements or capacity bounds, so the warning should be waived rather than repaired by self-assignments, dummy updates, or deletion of required guard logic.

The LNGDG3Covered to BatteryDischarge guard correctly represents dynamic EMS switching based on current external operating inputs. The NL gives no update semantics for those inputs inside the EMS controller, and the FixLog already contains a waiver for this same issue.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL edit made. The requested warnings concern intentional external-input/capacity reads in required forced classification guards; repairing them would require ungrounded input dynamics or deletion/simplification of preserved dispatch logic.

repair_rationale: All current requests are repeats of warnings already rejected/waived in the FixLog: W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for Pbat_max and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE for BatteryDischarge classification guards.
The NL explicitly says the EMS reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not specify internal dynamics for ship load, renewable production, SoC evolution, or Pbat_max.

repair_rationale: Fixed scenario low_soc_lng_dg3_dg1_adds_pd1_margin. Expected state was LNGShipEMS.LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC with Pg_req=100, Peng3_req=50, Pd1_req=60, Pd2_req=0, Pbat_charge=5, DG2_cut_in=0. The gap was in the forced classification guard, not in the state action: LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC already computes Pd1_req as PL-Ppv-Pw-Pgmax-eng3_Pmax+Pd1max/10 and Pbat_charge as Pd1max/10, which yields the expected 60 and 5 for the failing inputs.

The low-SoC DG1 charge guard now treats the Pd1max/10 charging margin as part of the margin-covered DG1 case, so PL=205 with Pgmax=100, eng3_Pmax=50, Pd1max=50 reaches LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC instead of falling through to all-thermal/DG2.

The all-thermal fallback remains preserved for genuine cases beyond the low-SoC DG1 margin-covered range, including DG2 last-priority dispatch and overload mitigation. All twelve required states, external input variables, cut command variables, RES full-SoC guards, and low-SoC charging margin actions are preserved.
Prior waived local/design warnings about external input variables are not re-fixed; this edit only changes the scenario-proven off-by-range classification for the low-SoC Pd1max/10 margin branch.

evidence.summary: The current hard request is the SD-6 simulation failure for scenario low_soc_lng_dg3_dg1_adds_pd1_margin. The failing step expected LNGShipEMS.LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC for PL=205, Ppv=0, Pw=0, SoC=0.2, Pgmax=100, eng3_Pmax=50, Pd1max=50, with Pg_req=100, Peng3_req=50, Pd1_req=60, Pd2_req=0, Pbat_charge=5, DG2_cut_in=0. The old guard required deficit + Pd1max/10 <= Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max, so deficit 205 fell through to AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation and cut in DG2. The candidate changes the guard to deficit <= Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd1max/10 and excludes that margin-covered low-SoC case from the all-thermal fallback, so the scenario now reaches the intended low-SoC DG1 charging branch whose existing enter action computes Pd1_req=205-100-50+5=60 and Pbat_charge=5.

The edit is narrowly scoped to the low-SoC DG1 charging-margin classification range. It preserves all twelve NL-required states, the external input/capacity variables PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pbat_max, Pgmax, eng3_Pmax, Pd1max, Pd2max, the dispatch output variables Pg_req, Peng3_req, Pd1_req, Pd2_req, Pbat_discharge, Pbat_charge, Pspare, and the cut-in/cut-out command variables. It does not delete the condition-classification architecture or invent unsupported internal dynamics for external operating inputs.

The FixLog shows prior SD-4 design warnings about unwritten external inputs and guard variables were repeatedly rejected with waiver because the NL explicitly says the FSM reads load, renewable, SoC, and capacity inputs and gives no internal update law. The present candidate does not attempt to repair those waived warnings; it only repairs new blocking scenario evidence. No local scenario regression is reported, and the scenario set previously had 17/18 passing with this one identified failure.

The local deterministic check rejects the candidate for missing_required_grounding of aggregate IDs rather than for parse, semantic, or scenario behavior. The candidate DSL concretely contains the relevant mechanisms, but under decomposed names and syntactic forms: individual unit cut commands LNG_cut_in/out, DG3_cut_in/out, DG1_cut_in/out, DG2_cut_in/out; load cut commands Load_cut_in/out; forced classification guards as the `! * -> ... : if [...]` transitions; RES/full-SoC guards in RESCoversCharge and RESCoversSpare; low-SoC charging-margin guards/actions in LNGCoveredChargeLowSoC, LNGDG3ChargeLowSoC, and LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC; and dispatch outputs through the state enter assignments to Pg_req, Peng3_req, Pd1_req, Pd2_req, Pbat_discharge, Pbat_charge, and Pspare.

local_override_rationale: Override SD-10 local rejection kind missing_required_grounding because the listed element IDs are aggregate grounding labels, while the DSL represents them compositionally. `variable:unit_cut_commands` is represented by LNG_cut_in/LNG_cut_out, DG3_cut_in/DG3_cut_out, DG1_cut_in/DG1_cut_out, and DG2_cut_in/DG2_cut_out in every state. `variable:load_cut_commands` is represented by Load_cut_in and Load_cut_out in every state. `transition:forced_classification_guards` is represented by the complete set of top-level forced `! * -> State : if [...]` transitions.

The locally reported missing guards are present in the candidate: `guard:res_covers_soc_full` is represented by the RESCoversCharge and RESCoversSpare guards using Ppv + Pw >= PL and SoC < 0.95 versus SoC >= 0.95; `guard:low_soc_charging_margins` is represented by the low-SoC Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10 margin guards and enter actions, including the repaired LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC guard. `action:dispatch_outputs` is represented by enter actions assigning requested generator power, battery charge/discharge, spare power, and cut commands in each dispatch state.

The major drift_risk reported by local evidence is therefore a grounding/matcher risk, not an NL-fidelity or scenario-regression finding. The NL and FixLog support the decomposed representation: the grounding_map assumptions already admit synthesized state names and coarse cut-command modeling, and the required preserve list asks for aggregate command/guard concepts rather than necessarily exact DSL identifiers. Passing this candidate is appropriate for the next full top-down revalidation pass, where target-level coverage can be re-audited without discarding the behaviorally fixed scenario.

decisions.rationale: The review provides new hard evidence that the all-thermal/overload state can be reached with unbounded battery discharge. I preserve the required AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation state but constrain its forced classification guard so any overload-lack battery discharge is bounded by Pbat_max and requires suitable SoC, while ordinary DG2-last-priority thermal coverage remains reachable.

accepted_edit_intent: Tighten LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC guard to require deficit + Pd1max / 10.0 <= Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max

decisions.rationale: The review shows the low-SoC LNG+DG3+DG1 charging branch can command Pd1_req above Pd1max because the guard allows the residual plus Pd1max/10 margin to exceed DG1 capacity. The smallest safe edit restores the guard to require the residual plus charging margin to fit within Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max, so the existing Pd1_req action cannot exceed Pd1max.

accepted_edit_intent: Repair the illegal/unbounded overload path by guarding battery-lack mitigation with SoC and Pbat_max

repair_rationale: Preserved all twelve required state declarations and all required input/output variables, including decomposed unit cut commands and load cut commands.

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: with PL=0, positive RES, and SoC below 0.95, first empty cycle dispatches to zero-load battery charging.
scenario_results.name: default_zero_load_res_charges_battery

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: with PL=0 and SoC at the 0.95 boundary, RES production should become spare power instead of battery charge.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_full_soc_routes_res_to_spare

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when RES exceeds positive load and SoC is just below 0.95, EMS should serve load from RES and charge the battery.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: at SoC=0.95 with RES exceeding load, residual renewable power should be spare, not battery charge.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_full_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when RES is below load, SoC is above low threshold, and deficit fits battery capacity, battery discharge should cover the gap before thermal units.
scenario_results.name: battery_supplies_deficit_when_soc_suitable

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: at SoC=0.2, LNG-covered deficit should include the Pgmax/5 charging margin while staying within LNG capacity.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_covered_adds_pgmax_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: just above low SoC, a deficit within LNG capacity should be covered by LNG without a battery charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_covers_deficit_above_low_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: at low SoC, when LNG alone is insufficient but LNG+DG3 plus Pd1max/10 margin suffices, EMS should use LNG and DG3 and charge the battery.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_dg3_adds_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: above low SoC, when deficit exceeds LNG but fits LNG+DG3, EMS should request LNG first and DG3 for the residual without charging.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg3_covers_deficit_above_low_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: at low SoC, when LNG+DG3 are insufficient but adding DG1 with Pd1max/10 margin suffices, EMS should use LNG, DG3, DG1, and charge.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_dg3_dg1_adds_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: above low SoC, when deficit exceeds LNG+DG3 but fits LNG+DG3+DG1, DG1 should be used as later priority without charging.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg3_dg1_covers_deficit_above_low_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: if demand exceeds RES and all thermal capacity, all thermal units should be active and remaining lack covered by battery discharge.
scenario_results.name: extreme_demand_all_thermal_and_battery_mitigation

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-transition probe: from the overload mitigation leaf, changed inputs with RES covering load and SoC at 0.95 must globally reclassify to RES spare; if the wildcard forced classification line is missing, the state would incorrectly remain in overload.
scenario_results.name: forced_reclassification_escapes_overload_to_res_spare

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-transition probe: from ZeroLoadCharge, changed positive-load inputs with suitable SoC and battery capacity must globally reclassify to BatteryDischarge; if the wildcard forced classification line is missing, the state would incorrectly remain in zero-load charging.
scenario_results.name: forced_reclassification_from_zero_load_to_battery

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-transition probe: from RESCoversSpare, changed high-deficit inputs that exceed LNG+DG3 but fit LNG+DG3+DG1 must globally reclassify to LNGDG3DG1Covered; missing forced classification would leave the old RES-spare state active.
scenario_results.name: forced_reclassification_from_res_spare_to_lng_dg3_dg1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-transition probe: from LNGDG3Covered, changed zero-load full-SoC inputs must globally reclassify to ZeroLoadSpare; missing wildcard classification would leave the thermal state active.
scenario_results.name: forced_reclassification_from_lng_dg3_to_zero_load_spare

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-transition probe: from BatteryDischarge, changed low-SoC LNG-covered inputs must globally reclassify to LNGCoveredChargeLowSoC; missing wildcard classification would leave battery-only dispatch active.
scenario_results.name: forced_reclassification_from_battery_to_lng_low_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-transition probe: from RESCoversSpare, changed inputs with PL=0, positive RES, and SoC below 0.95 must globally reclassify to ZeroLoadCharge; if the ZeroLoadCharge wildcard forced classification line is missing, the state would incorrectly remain in RES-spare.
scenario_results.name: forced_reclassification_to_zero_load_charge

evidence.summary: The candidate directly addresses all three hard SL-7 requests. For fixreq-3-sl7-0, the AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation forced guard now requires demand to be no more than total thermal capacity plus Pbat_max and requires SoC > 0.2 for the beyond-thermal battery-lack case, eliminating the previously unbounded battery discharge path while preserving ordinary DG2-covered all-thermal operation. For fixreq-3-sl7-1, the LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC guard now requires deficit + Pd1max/10 <= Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max, so the state action Pd1_req = residual + Pd1max/10 cannot exceed Pd1max. For fixreq-3-sl7-2, those same edits repair the two root NL-fidelity failures behind the quality cap.

The NL requires the EMS to read capacity bounds and dispatch within generating-unit capacity semantics; the SL-7 blocking review specifically identified the old low-SoC DG1-margin behavior as a capacity violation because Pd1_req became 60 when Pd1max was 50. The candidate’s tightened guard is therefore NL-fidelity improving even though it invalidates the prior simulation oracle case that expected Pd1_req=60.

The candidate preserves the twelve required states, the external operating/capacity inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pbat_max, Pgmax, eng3_Pmax, Pd1max, and Pd2max, the dispatch outputs Pg_req, Peng3_req, Pd1_req, Pd2_req, Pbat_discharge, Pbat_charge, and Pspare, the decomposed unit and load cut commands, RES/full-SoC branches, forced classification guards, and low-SoC charging-margin mechanisms. No required NL element is deleted.

The FixLog shows earlier local/design objections about unwritten external inputs and aggregate grounding were waived or overridden because the NL models these quantities as read inputs and the DSL represents aggregate concepts compositionally. The current candidate does not reopen those waived issues; it only makes the new SL-7 hard-blocking safety/capacity edits.

local_override_rationale: Override the SD-10 scenario_regression finding because the failing scenario low_soc_lng_dg3_dg1_adds_pd1_margin expects the exact behavior newly rejected by SL-7 as a hard NL-fidelity defect: with PL=205, Ppv=0, Pw=0, SoC=0.2, Pgmax=100, eng3_Pmax=50, and Pd1max=50, the old oracle expected LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC with Pd1_req=60 and DG2 off. SL-7 found that commanding DG1 above Pd1max conflicts with capacity-bound dispatch. The candidate correctly prevents that branch by requiring deficit + Pd1max/10 <= Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max; the local scenario failure is therefore an obsolete-oracle regression, not a real NL-fidelity regression.

For the same failed scenario, the candidate’s actual state AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation with Pg_req=100, Peng3_req=50, Pd1_req=50, Pd2_req=5, Pbat_charge=0, and DG2 cut in is consistent with the accepted repair intent: DG1 is capped at Pd1max and DG2 is used only after LNG, DG3, and DG1 are exhausted. This preserves priority ordering better than the previous over-capacity DG1 command.

The current local drift_risk=major is driven by the obsolete scenario expectation plus the already-overridden aggregate grounding matcher, not by parse, semantic, or newly demonstrated NL-fidelity loss. Given the hard SL-7 capacity/safety requests and the candidate diff, passing to the next full top-down revalidation is justified so the scenario oracle can be re-audited against the corrected capacity-bound interpretation.

local_override_rationale: Override the SD-10 scenario_regression finding because the failing scenario low_soc_lng_dg3_dg1_adds_pd1_margin expects the exact behavior newly rejected by SL-7 as a hard NL-fidelity defect: with PL=205, Ppv=0, Pw=0, SoC=0.2, Pgmax=100, eng3_Pmax=50, and Pd1max=50, the old oracle expected LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC with Pd1_req=60 and DG2 off. SL-7 found that commanding DG1 above Pd1max conflicts with capacity-bound dispatch. The candidate correctly prevents that branch by requiring deficit + Pd1max/10 <= Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max; the local scenario failure is therefore an obsolete-oracle regression, not a real NL-fidelity regression.

For the same failed scenario, the candidate’s actual state AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation with Pg_req=100, Peng3_req=50, Pd1_req=50, Pd2_req=5, Pbat_charge=0, and DG2 cut in is consistent with the accepted repair intent: DG1 is capped at Pd1max and DG2 is used only after LNG, DG3, and DG1 are exhausted. This preserves priority ordering better than the previous over-capacity DG1 command.

Override the repeated SD-10 missing_required_grounding objection for variable:unit_cut_commands, variable:load_cut_commands, transition:forced_classification_guards, guard:res_covers_soc_full, guard:low_soc_charging_margins, and action:dispatch_outputs because the FixLog repair_memory already documents that these are aggregate matcher labels represented compositionally in the DSL. Unit commands are represented by LNG_cut_in/out, DG3_cut_in/out, DG1_cut_in/out, and DG2_cut_in/out; load commands by Load_cut_in/out; forced classification by the top-level `! * -> ... : if [...]` guards; RES full-SoC guards by RESCoversCharge/RESCoversSpare conditions; low-SoC margins by Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10 guards/actions; and dispatch outputs by each state’s enter assignments.

The current local drift_risk=major is driven by the obsolete scenario expectation plus the already-overridden aggregate grounding matcher, not by parse, semantic, or newly demonstrated NL-fidelity loss. Given the hard SL-7 capacity/safety requests and the candidate diff, passing to the next full top-down revalidation is justified so the scenario oracle can be re-audited against the corrected capacity-bound interpretation.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Add Pbat_max and SoC limits to the AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation forced guard for demand beyond total thermal capacity', 'Keep DG2-covered all-thermal operation reachable when the deficit is within Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max']
decisions.rationale: The review provides new hard evidence that the all-thermal/overload state can be reached with unbounded battery discharge. I preserve the required AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation state but constrain its forced classification guard so any overload-lack battery discharge is bounded by Pbat_max and requires suitable SoC, while ordinary DG2-last-priority thermal coverage remains reachable.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Tighten LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC guard to require deficit + Pd1max / 10.0 <= Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max', 'Align the LNGDG3DG1Covered and all-thermal exclusions with the tightened low-SoC DG1 margin condition']
decisions.rationale: The review shows the low-SoC LNG+DG3+DG1 charging branch can command Pd1_req above Pd1max because the guard allows the residual plus Pd1max/10 margin to exceed DG1 capacity. The smallest safe edit restores the guard to require the residual plus charging margin to fit within Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max, so the existing Pd1_req action cannot exceed Pd1max.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Repair the illegal/unbounded overload path by guarding battery-lack mitigation with SoC and Pbat_max', 'Repair the DG1 over-capacity path by constraining the low-SoC DG1 charging-margin guard']
decisions.rationale: The nfrr_quality_cap is a root-cause quality finding over the same two unsafe behaviors: combined reachable overload recovery and generator over-capacity. The accepted edits repair those underlying NL-fidelity issues without deleting required states, variables, forced classification guards, low-SoC margin concepts, or dispatch actions.

diff_summary.summary: Tightened the low-SoC LNG+DG3+DG1 charging guard and matching exclusions so DG1 cannot be commanded above Pd1max. Added SoC and Pbat_max constraints to the AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation forced guard for demand exceeding total thermal capacity, while preserving DG2-covered operation within thermal capacity.

repair_rationale: Preserved all twelve required state declarations and all required input/output variables, including decomposed unit cut commands and load cut commands.
Addressed fixreq-3-sl7-1 by tightening the LNGDG3DG1ChargeLowSoC guard so Pd1_req = residual + Pd1max/10 can only run when that value is within Pd1max.

Addressed fixreq-3-sl7-0 by retaining the all-thermal state for DG2 last-priority and bounded overload mitigation, but preventing unbounded battery discharge: overload residual beyond thermal capacity must be no greater than Pbat_max and requires SoC > 0.2.

Addressed fixreq-3-sl7-2 by repairing the root NL-fidelity issues rather than reworking waived external-input warnings. PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pgmax, eng3_Pmax, Pd1max, Pd2max, and Pbat_max remain external operating/capacity inputs read by classification guards.

The previously overridden aggregate-grounding local objection remains audit-only: unit_cut_commands are represented by LNG/DG cut-in/out variables, load_cut_commands by Load_cut_in/out, forced_classification_guards by top-level forced guard transitions, and dispatch_outputs by each state's enter assignments.

repair_rationale: Accepted both hard SL-7 requests because they provide new review evidence about the illegal overload behavior, not a waived aggregate-grounding or stale-scenario objection.

For fixreq-4-sl7-0, the gap was that AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation looked like an ordinary successful dispatch. The candidate adds overload_illegal and sets it to 1 when PL - Ppv - Pw exceeds Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max, making the illegal condition explicit while preserving the required state.

For fixreq-4-sl7-1, the gap was that the extreme-demand recovery kept Load_cut_in = 1 and Load_cut_out = 0 while using battery discharge for over-thermal lack. The candidate changes only the over-thermal branch to Load_cut_in = 0 and Load_cut_out = 1; within-thermal DG2-last-priority dispatch remains Load_cut_in = 1.

The existing bounded guard for AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation is preserved: over-thermal battery lack remains constrained by Pbat_max and SoC > 0.2, so the repair does not reintroduce the previously rejected unbounded battery-discharge path.

All twelve required states, external input variables, dispatch output variables, decomposed unit/load cut commands, forced classification guards, RES/full-SoC guards, and low-SoC charging-margin guards/actions are preserved.

evidence.summary: Both hard SL-7 requests are resolved by the candidate diff. local_override_rationale: Override SD-10 local rejection kind scenario_regression because the sole current failed scenario, extreme_demand_all_thermal_and_battery_mitigation, is asserting the obsolete behavior that SL-7 just rejected: a beyond-total-thermal overload remains load-cut-in normal service. The candidate’s actual behavior for PL=230 with total thermal 225 and Pbat_max=10 is NL- and FixLog-consistent: it remains in AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation, activates the thermal units, computes the battery-covered lack, but marks the condition illegal and performs fail-safe load cut-out. That is the accepted repair intent for fixreq-4-sl7-0 and fixreq-4-sl7-1, not a real NL-fidelity regression.

The local oracle expected Load_cut_in=1 and no explicit illegal diagnostic for a demand that exceeds all RES and thermal resources. The NL states that this overload completion condition is illegal and shall never occur in practice, and the current hard requests specifically required a diagnostic, rejection, or fail-safe load-shedding action. Therefore the candidate’s Load_cut_in=0, Load_cut_out=1, and overload_illegal=1 are justified overrides of the local scenario expectation.

Override the repeated missing_required_grounding objection for variable:unit_cut_commands, variable:load_cut_commands, transition:forced_classification_guards, guard:res_covers_soc_full, guard:low_soc_charging_margins, and action:dispatch_outputs for the same reason recorded in prior repair_memory. These are aggregate matcher labels represented compositionally in the DSL: unit cut commands are LNG_cut_in/out, DG3_cut_in/out, DG1_cut_in/out, and DG2_cut_in/out; load commands are Load_cut_in/out; forced classification is the top-level set of ! * -> State guards; RES/full-SoC guards are the RESCoversCharge/RESCoversSpare and zero-load SoC guards; low-SoC margins are Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10 guard/action pairs; dispatch outputs are assigned in each state enter block.

The FixLog shows these aggregate grounding objections were already overridden as audit-only, and the current candidate does not delete or weaken those represented mechanisms. The current local drift_risk=major is driven by an obsolete overload-service oracle plus the repeated aggregate grounding matcher limitation, not by parse failure, semantic failure, or a new loss of NL-required states/events/guards/actions.

decisions.rationale: The unsafe recovery evidence shows the extreme-demand case silently keeps loads cut in while using battery discharge for over-thermal lack. The smallest safe edit is to keep the NL-grounded all-thermal activation and bounded battery-lack computation, but add explicit illegal-state signaling and fail-safe load cut-out when deficit exceeds all thermal resources. diff_summary.summary: Added an overload_illegal diagnostic flag, reset it in normal dispatch states, and changed AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation so demand within total thermal capacity remains normal DG2-last-priority service while demand beyond total thermal capacity is explicitly marked illegal/fail-safe with Load_cut_in = 0 and Load_cut_out = 1.

repair_rationale: Accepted both hard SL-7 requests because they provide new review evidence about the illegal overload behavior, not a waived aggregate-grounding or stale-scenario objection.

For fixreq-4-sl7-0, the gap was that AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation looked like an ordinary successful dispatch. The candidate adds overload_illegal and sets it to 1 when PL - Ppv - Pw exceeds Pgmax + eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max, making the illegal condition explicit while preserving the required state.

For fixreq-4-sl7-1, the gap was that the extreme-demand recovery kept Load_cut_in = 1 and Load_cut_out = 0 while using battery discharge for over-thermal lack. The candidate changes only the over-thermal branch to Load_cut_in = 0 and Load_cut_out = 1; within-thermal DG2-last-priority dispatch remains Load_cut_in = 1.

The existing bounded guard for AllThermalAndOverloadMitigation is preserved: over-thermal battery lack remains constrained by Pbat_max and SoC > 0.2, so the repair does not reintroduce the previously rejected unbounded battery-discharge path.

All twelve required states, external input variables, dispatch output variables, decomposed unit/load cut commands, forced classification guards, RES/full-SoC guards, and low-SoC charging-margin guards/actions are preserved.
